items.title: Campaigners back call for scrutiny of consent laws by Joanne Young
items.author: Emine Sinmaz and Alexandra Topping
items.content:
Experts say no law states third-party consent is a valid defence and call for public debate and further education

Campaigners have welcomed a call for scrutiny of consent laws by a survivor of drug-facilitated rape but said action must also focus on wider issues around sexual assault.

Joanne Young, who was drugged and raped by her husband and sexually abused by men he invited into their home, warned of “serious questions about how the law deals with consent”.

Continue reading...

items.title: On the Trail With Spain’s Prime Minister, as He Tries to Pull Out a Win
items.author: Jason Horowitz
items.content: <article>Pedro Sánchez, Europe’s most prominent left-wing leader, seems set to lose power in an election next week. Our reporter trailed his last-ditch effort to turn his campaign around.</article>

items.title: ‘So what if there’s a hole? It hasn’t collapsed’: Kyiv residents unbothered by Russian attacks on city’s bridges
items.author: Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv; photographs by Julia Kochetova
items.content:
Despite dodging tears in the tarmac, people are confident in city’s infrastructure – and will not worry about what has not happened yet

Mykola expects to drive his battered beige passenger minibus 20 to 24 times a day past the holes in the road on Kyiv’s damaged Northern Bridge that were caused by a Russian ballistic missile attack on Tuesday.

Buses are now the only motor transport allowed across the normally busy multi-lane crossing, though on their way into the city centre they have to skirt the tears in the tarmac, using the only functioning lane to get by.

Continue reading...

items.title: Tourists are throwing fewer coins into Rome’s Trevi fountain – is €2 entry fee to blame?
items.author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
items.content:
Charity that collects the coins says donations are down by £200,000 after a barrier was put in place to restrict access

When Jeff Clinton, an American visiting Rome with his wife for the first time, found a US one-cent coin on a street close to Termini train station, he knew precisely what he was going to do with it. “I’ll throw it into the Trevi fountain,” said Clinton, holding the copper coin in the palm of his hand as the couple admired the landmark.

He was well aware of the tradition among tourists of tossing a coin over their shoulder and into the waters of the baroque masterpiece, in a ritual fabled to ensure a return visit to the city or make other dreams come true.

Continue reading...

items.title: Teenager allegedly organised arsons and kidnapping on Signal during Melbourne hospitality wars
items.author: Nino Bucci
items.content:
Victoria police say boy, 17, communicated with offenders under username ‘Onepercent’

Victorian police allege a 17-year-old boy tasked others to carry out a series of arsons, home invasions and a mistaken identity kidnapping that resulted in the partial amputation of a victim’s finger during Melbourne’s hospitality wars.

The boy, who was arrested on Friday afternoon, allegedly communicated with the offenders under the username “Onepercent” on the encrypted communications app Signal.

Continue reading...

items.title: When you see smoke, run: Rohingya who escaped Myanmar’s genocide tell their stories
items.author: Kaamil Ahmed
items.content:
Survivors recount rivers red with blood and burning nearby villages serving as an urgent warning to flee their homes

Smoke was often the signal to run – seen from a distance, it was the indication for Rohingya that a neighbouring village was under attack and that theirs would be next.

In other places, they saw the rivers run red and would pull out the bodies, perform quick burial rites and then flee.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘A new record for entertainment’: Grand Theft Auto VI sales hit $3.8bn on first day of release, developer says
items.author: Guardian staff and agencies
items.content:
The announcement from Rockstar Games would mean GTA VI has already earned more than the entire box office run of the highest-grossing film of all time

Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games has announced, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.

The worldwide figure was based on company estimates through the end of the day Thursday, the day the game launched. Rockstar said also it had sold 32.5m units of the game on prerelease, setting a record across platforms.

Continue reading...

items.title: Judge Approves $7 Billion Settlement Over Claims That Roundup Caused Cancer
items.author: Kevin Draper
items.content: <article>The ruling, in a nationwide class-action suit, is expected to end tens of thousands of lawsuits by people claiming that Roundup caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma.</article>

items.title: Trump Administration Says Army Can Blow Up Lead-Laced Explosives
items.author: Quinn Glabicki, John Ismay and Hiroko Tabuchi
items.content: <article>The detonation, now set for Monday, could create a cloud of lead dust stretching for miles over homes and farms, the Army has said. Environmental groups are seeking an emergency stay.</article>

items.title: Playing ‘Key of Life,’ Stevie Wonder Invites All to Match His Joy
items.author: Wesley Morris
items.content: <article>Wonder’s optimism was refracted around Madison Square Garden as he performed his “Songs in the Key of Life” album on a 50th anniversary tour.</article>

items.title: Fiona the Hippo Died After Eating a Hat. Some Want Justice.
items.author: Jessica Contrera, Remy Tumin and Kevin Williams
items.content: <article>Social media commenters have called for investigations, the release of zoo video footage and punishment for the parents of a child whose hat Fiona ingested.</article>

items.title: Man accused of sparking deadly Los Angeles wildfire found guilty
items.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
items.content:
Verdict in case against former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht comes after first trial ended with hung jury

The 30-year-old accused of sparking the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles was found guilty of two federal arson charges in a Friday verdict that came months after his first trial concluded with a hung jury.

For two weeks, a fresh batch of jurors listened to prosecutors mount their case against Jonathan Rinderknecht.

Continue reading...

items.title: Jury in Palisades Fire Trial Finds Man Guilty of Arson in Devastating Blaze
items.author: Tim Arango and Vik Jolly
items.content: <article>The defendant, Jonathan Rinderknecht, was found guilty on two counts. The verdict provides a measure of accountability for a painful chapter in recent L.A. history.</article>

items.title: Nvidia Said to Face S.E.C. Probe Into Its Accounting Practices
items.author: Lauren Hirsch, Matthew Goldstein and Jessica Silver-Greenberg
items.content: <article>Questions around the company’s accounting had surfaced amid revelations about its questionable chip sales in Asia.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Mathematician Claims to Solve Riemann Hypothesis With Help From Claude
items.author: Kenneth Chang and Siobhan Roberts
items.content: <article>If confirmed, the proof of the Riemann hypothesis would cement the field’s sense that no unsolved problem is safe from artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: Victorian Greens seek urgent injunction over how-to-vote cards mimicking party’s branding but preferencing it last
items.author: Henry Belot
items.content:
Independent candidate Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s cards instruct people to vote in a way that would benefit Liberal party

The Victorian Greens are seeking an urgent injunction from the supreme court to stop an independent candidate distributing how-to-vote cards that allegedly mimic the party’s branding and urge people to preference it last.

As prepoll opened on Wednesday morning, Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s campaign team handed out how-to-vote cards that used the minor party’s colour scheme, font and triangle logo with the banner “Vote 1 Green Values”.

Continue reading...

items.title: Trump turns White House press conference into a 2028 succession audition
items.author: David Smith in Washington
items.content:
The president appeared to put Vance and Rubio through their paces as potential successors, though Stephen Miller unexpectedly stole the spotlight

“Which of you shall we say doth love us most?”

The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘A source of inspiration’: California celebrates the late civil rights icon Dolores Huerta
items.author: Maria G Ortiz-Briones
items.content:
A public vigil and celebration of life honor the civil rights activist and co-founder of United Farm Workers union

Hundreds of people came out to honor and celebrate the life and legacy of the California civil rights activist Dolores Huerta at a celebration-of-life event Friday in Bakersfield.

Huerta’s daughter Lori de Leon thanked attendees for their support during her mother’s passing, highlighting the widespread tributes and communities gathering in her honor.

Continue reading...

items.title: Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial
items.author: Robert Mackey
items.content:
Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’

Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump’s nominee to lead a key US cybersecurity agency, Michael LoSapio, after he denied during a hearing that the Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021.

Tillis, who declined to run for re-election and after repeated clashes with Trump’s, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination to serve as a director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (Cisa). His block on the nomination will prevent it from being included in a package of nominees to be voted on next month, before the Republicans lose their majority in the Senate.

Continue reading...

items.title: NSW passes Mount Pleasant coalmine law as Greens claim change an attempt to head off One Nation
items.author: Penry Buckley and Lisa Cox
items.content:
Labor says allowing mine to increase production reflects ‘gravity of situation facing hundreds of workers’ – but critics call it ‘unprecedented and dangerous’

The New South Wales government has passed special legislation to allow a coalmine in the Hunter Valley to increase production by 32% in its final act of parliament before the March state election, in which the region will be a key battleground for One Nation.

After a marathon session in the legislative council on Friday, the Minns government and the Coalition voted at 1.36am on Saturday morning to allow the Mount Pleasant mine to increase its annual extraction rate from 12.5MT to 16.5MT until 2032.

Continue reading...

items.title: What Is a Stock Market Correction?
items.author: Aruni Soni
items.content: <article>The S&P 500 has fallen more than 10 percent from its recent high, crossing a threshold that signals investors have turned pessimistic about stocks.</article>

items.title: Stocks Skid Into a Correction, as A.I. Worries Intensify
items.author: Joe Rennison
items.content: <article>The S&P 500 ended the day down more than 10 percent from its recent high, in a symbolic measure of investors’ souring mood.</article>

items.title: California Storm Forecast to Hit Thanksgiving Week Amid High King Tides
items.author: Amy Graff
items.content: <article>“We could have flooding in areas where we have never seen flooding before,” a forecaster with the National Weather Service said.</article>

items.title: French police officers found guilty of racist assault on black music producer
items.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
items.content:
Beating of Michel Zecler in 2020 sparked outrage over police brutality after it was caught on security cameras

Three French police officers who beat a black music producer they said was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic have been found guilty of intentional, racist violence.

The brutal assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, was caught on security cameras in his building in 2020 and triggered outrage in France over police brutality. The trial this month was considered a turning point for the recognition of racist violence.

Continue reading...

items.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad
items.author: Ben Doherty
items.content:
President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi

Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan.

In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.

Continue reading...

items.title: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading
items.author: Lauren Almeida and Graeme Wearden
items.content:
The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout

As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory.

Continue reading...

items.title: John Grisham: Scott Colom Makes Me Proud of Mississippi
items.author: John Grisham
items.content: <article>As a kid, I once watched the Ku Klux Klan burn a cross in my hometown in Mississippi. Sixty years later, I look forward to shaking Mr. Colom’s hand and telling him I’m proud he’s my senator.</article>

items.title: How Do You Investigate a President This Corrupt?
items.author: Ezra Klein and Jack McCordick
items.content: <article>The incoming House Oversight Committee chairman, Robert Garcia, lays out his committee’s top targets.</article>

items.title: As a Storm Floods Florida, Heavy Rain Will Creep Up the East Coast
items.author: Judson Jones
items.content: <article>A potential tropical storm off the coast of Florida is expected to move up the coast and could snarl Thanksgiving week travel.</article>

items.title: JP Morgan boss says he will find ways to offset ‘unfair’ rise in UK tax on banks
items.author: Alex Daniel
items.content:
Jamie Dimon says he is ‘setting an example’ in seeking to claw back Labour’s increase in surcharge, from 3% to 6%

Jamie Dimon, the chief executive of JP Morgan, has said he will find ways to offset the chancellor’s tax rise for banks, calling the increase unfair.

Speaking at an event in London on Thursday, Dimon said he would seek to claw back the increase and was “setting an example so that [governments] understand the trade-offs of these unfair penalties”.

Continue reading...

items.title: Police arrest teacher who missed sentencing after indecent assault conviction
items.author: Caroline Davies
items.content:
Sally-Anne Bowen was found guilty of having sexual relationships with two pupils at a boys’ school in the 1980s

A chemistry teacher who had sexual relationships with two pupils at a boys’ school in the late 1980s has been arrested by police in Hampshire after she failed to turn up to her sentencing hearing.

Sally-Anne Bowen, 65, could not be found at her home by Metropolitan police officers on Friday morning after a warrant was issued for her arrest, a court heard.

Continue reading...

items.title: Florida mechanic found guilty of murdering British woman who attorney says came to US to die
items.author: Edward Helmore
items.content:
Dwain Hall was convicted of stabbing Sonia Exelby, a music teacher who prosecutors say suffered from mental illness

A Florida mechanic has been found guilty of stabbing to death a British music teacher, whom he convinced to travel to the United States.

Dwain Hall, an auto repair and tow truck driver, groomed 32-year-old Sonia Exelby from Portsmouth, England, on a fetish website before luring her to the US.

Continue reading...

items.title: Spain frees wealthy US-sought activist on bail as Irish police raid Dublin home
items.author: Timothy Pratt
items.content:
Pro-Palestinian donor James ‘Fergie’ Chambers released as court considers extradition request

In a blur of events surrounding the Trump administration’s effort to extradite James “Fergie” Chambers, Spain released the wealthy US activist and donor on bail even as Irish police raided a Dublin house owned by Chambers and his partner, Stella Schnabel, acting on a request from US authorities.

Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.

Continue reading...

items.title: Indian man sentenced to 19 years in prison for conspiring to kill Sikh separatist in New York
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Nikhil Gupta admitted to plotting with Indian government official to hire hitman to murder dual US-Canadian citizen

An Indian ⁠man was sentenced to more ⁠than 19 ​years in US prison on Friday after admitting to orchestrating a failed Indian government-backed plot to kill a Sikh separatist in New York ⁠City, in connection with what US and Canadian authorities have called a broader effort to target Indian dissidents.

Nikhil Gupta, 55, pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy ⁠to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

Continue reading...

items.title: Misty-eyed Burnham gambles on closer ties with EU as he throws down gauntlet to Tories and Reform
items.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
items.content:
PM challenges rivals to rebuff plan he says could add 0.5% annual growth to economy and offer young people hope

Several sentences into a slightly convoluted answer about where UK-EU relations might go next, Andy Burnham abruptly changed tack. “The important point is that the Britain of today and the EU of today is not the one of 2016,” he said. “Life has moved on in so many ways.”

This is undoubtedly true. But Burnham’s political gamble on closer ties with Brussels hinges on the assumption that most British voters feel this way as well.

Continue reading...

items.title: Two men killed after glider crashes into Loch Leven in Scotland
items.author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
items.content:
The pair had taken off from the Scottish Gliding Centre at nearby Portmoak on a training flight

Two men have been killed after their glider crashed into Loch Leven, a large body of water in Perth and Kinross, on Friday morning.

Police Scotland said their bodies were recovered from the loch by the emergency services after the alarm was raised at 11.05am on Friday.

Continue reading...

items.title: As the Coalition stares down One Nation in NSW, a new threat is rising: the teals
items.author: Anne Davies
items.content:
The opposition’s struggle is creating an opportunity for progressive independents who are boosted by shrewd political operator Chris Minns

The New South Wales Coalition is facing a renewed threat to its heartland seats on Sydney’s north shore.

This time, the threat is from independent candidates – and they’re backed by the same community activists who put a swathe of teal independents into federal parliament.

Continue reading...

items.title: US reacts cautiously to Myanmar genocide ruling as EU praises ‘critical’ role of UN’s top court
items.author: Jason Burke
items.content:
Reactions to ICJ ruling underline global divisions over court with China raising concerns about judicial overreach

The US has greeted with caution the world’s highest court’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, while China has raised concerns of judicial overreach.

Reactions to Thursday’s historic ruling underlined deep international division over the role of the court and similar institutions. The international court of justice (ICJ) had never previously found a state responsible for genocide and the decision could set a precedent for future genocide claims, notably a case against Israel.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Weak and dizzy’: the secretive ICE force-feeding tactics that ended a Cuban father’s hunger strike
items.author: José Olivares
items.content:
Exclusive: Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez says in messages to Guardian from inside Texas facility pain of force-feeding caused him to break strike

The text message that came from inside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center was stark: “I have spent five days eating regular food. If I don’t eat it, they put the tube in me to feed me.”

A Cuban asylum seeker, Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez, 32, said in messages to the Guardian this month that he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating, but that he had broken his hunger strike because being force-fed was just too painful.

Continue reading...

items.title: California investigates Nvidia over whether chip exports ended up in China
items.author: Mark Sweney
items.content:
State attorney says scandal ‘raises bright red flags’ and aims to find out if company misled investors

California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang.

Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based company’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions.

Continue reading...

items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.author: Alice Nightingale-Smith for MetDesk
items.content:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

Continue reading...

items.title: Vape users hospitalised after losing consciousness, prompting public health warning in New South Wales
items.author: Catie McLeod
items.content:
Testing confirms presence of etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but not registered for medical use in Australia

Three people who lost consciousness and were hospitalised in New South Wales after using certain vapes have tested positive for the unregulated anaesthetic agent etomidate, health officials said.

NSW health on Friday issued a public warning about vape liquids containing etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but not registered for medical use in Australia.

Continue reading...

items.title: Race to be next UN secretary general exposes divisions among world powers
items.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic Editor
items.content:
Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner

The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.

Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.

Continue reading...

items.title: Iraq university’s removal of male professors teaching women sparks weeks of protests
items.author: Ali Aziz, Maria Talal and Tom Levitt
items.content:
Al-Qadisiyah University’s move a sign of the country’s slide into a Taliban-like gender segregation, say activists

The removal of male professors teaching female students at a university in southern Iraq has sparked protests and been criticised by activists as a Taliban-like gender segregation policy.

As many as 400 women are estimated to have joined protests over the past two weeks calling for the return of their professors at Al-Qadisiyah University in a move that appears to have surprised its administrators.

Continue reading...

items.title: Myanmar ruling gives new relevance to genocide convention and is ‘full of messages’ for Israel
items.author: Julian Borger
items.content:
Hailed as ‘a rare moment of justice’, judges’ decision sets out a roadmap for assessing the question of intent

In their nine votes to six majority ruling, the panel of judges in The Hague set out a detailed roadmap for how the convention should be applied to real-world situations in which a government is accused of committing genocide against a whole population group, especially when it comes to assessing the question of intent.

Continue reading...

items.title: China, Russia and US agree peace declaration with no mention of Ukraine and Iran wars
items.author: Rebecca Bailey in Shenzhen
items.content:
Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’

China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants.

The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it said was the protection of diplomatic immunity.

Continue reading...

items.title: Trump accused of falling asleep during Xi Jinping speech at Apec summit in China
items.author: Ariana Baio
items.content:
US president appeared to doze off while Chinese leader made speech, but White House insisted he was awake

The US president appeared to close his eyes for roughly 10 seconds on Thursday. As his eyes closed, Trump’s head tilted downward, and his hands remained clasped in front of him.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Everyone struggled for this justice’: tears in court as Rohingya vindicated in Myanmar genocide ruling
items.author: Kaamil Ahmed in The Hague and Yassin Abdumonab in Cox's Bazar
items.content:
Relief in the immediate aftermath of a landmark ruling, but what happens next is in the hands of governments around the world

There were tears in the halls of The Hague in the Netherlands and an eruption of applause in the refugee camps of Bangladesh as the scattered communities of Rohingya watched the UN’s top court rule the Myanmar military had committed genocide against them.

For almost a decade, the Rohingya have awaited this moment; recognition from the international court of justice (ICJ) that Myanmar in 2017 intentionally tried to destroy the mostly Muslim minority group through a campaign of mass killings and rape. More than 10,000 Rohingya were killed and 700,000 fled to neighbouring Bangladesh.

Continue reading...

items.title: Politics
Business
Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules
items.author: Kaamil Ahmed in The Hague, and Oliver Holmes
items.content:
Judgment finds ‘intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population’ after case seen as critical test for dealing with most serious of state crimes

Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 military campaign, the world’s highest court has ruled, in a historic and unprecedented decision.

The judgment from the international court of justice (ICJ) – which has never previously found a state responsible for genocide – ends a seven-year legal battle that was seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.

Continue reading...

items.title: Israeli tanks cross ‘yellow line’ boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza
items.author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
items.content:
First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu

The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.

Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road, Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.

Continue reading...

items.title: Eight injured after driver in Israel repeatedly rams car into Palestinians
items.author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
items.content:
Arab MPs accuse politicians of fuelling hostility as footage shows driver accelerating towards Palestinians at four locations in Kafr Qasim

Eight people were injured on Wednesday evening when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel.

Footage shared on social media appears to show the car accelerating towards people, all Palestinians, at several locations in the city, striking them before driving away. Three of those injured were in moderate condition, and several of the victims were women leaving a nearby wedding, the Times of Israel reported.

Continue reading...

items.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
items.author: Rebecca Ratcliffe
items.content:
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits

Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

Continue reading...

items.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
items.author: Sarah Johnson
items.content:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

Continue reading...

items.title: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse

A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.

Continue reading...

items.title: Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military
items.author: Tom Phillips Latin America correspondent
items.content:
Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago

Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.

Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

items.title: Israel delays building contracts for West Bank settlement after UK sanctions
items.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
items.content:
Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu

Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.

Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street. Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, said any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever new administration was formed.

items.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
items.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
items.content:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

items.title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
items.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
items.content:
Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans

The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.

The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

items.title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats
items.author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
items.content:
St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access

The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.

On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.
